items.text: The final gasp of winter snow falls, eventually giving way to clear skies.
For this impoverished village, such a celebration is rare. Every household gathers in Master Hú's courtyard, drinking deeply and eating meat by the mouthful.
Rumor has it that this is all thanks to Doctor Xiù's mediation, marking it a feast to celebrate the slaying of the tiger and to pray for a plentiful harvest in the year to come.

items.speaker: Hunter
items.text: Make way! Our young hero is here!

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: A toast to you, my friend!
The moment Chéng steps into the courtyard, several hunters block his way with raised bowls of wine.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: There's no need for that. I merely did what I could.

items.speaker: Hunter
items.text: There's no need to be so polite! Come, sit, have a drink with us! It'd be rude not to.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I don't care for drinking.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: Drink! Drink! Drink!

items.speaker: Hunter
items.text: Yeah! Go on!
Doctor Xiù hides behind a nearby pillar, quietly chuckling to herself.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Hah. Hopefully that will get him to loosen up a bit.

items.speaker: Little Girl
items.text: Doctor! Doctor! My belly hurts!
A little girl tugs at the doctor's sleeve, looking up at her with tear-filled eyes.
She squats down, presses gentle fingers on her pulse, and slips a sugar-bound pill into her hand.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: It's nothing to worry over, child. Take this sweet little pill, and you'll feel better in no time.

items.speaker: Little Girl
items.text: Thank you, Doctor!
Doctor Xiù lifts her eyes to see a deep-blue-clad figure sitting along the edge of the black roof tiles.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: That boy ... Can he really not enjoy any sort of celebration?
She climbs the ladder up to the eaves, one step at a time.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: *sigh* Even I need a ladder to get up to the roof these days.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: There are too many people down there. I did only my duty. There's no need for all this gratitude.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I saw the tiger fall into a ravine. How was it able to survive?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Such things are rare, but not unheard of.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Perhaps it was not a tiger at all, but instead a beast possessed, controlled by some arcane means, or perhaps it was some manner of mindless spirit.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I heard once that, a long time ago, a horse once jumped off a cliff only to find a great fortune, even ascending to immortality!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Please!
Doctor Xiù opens her wine jar and sits cross-legged beside him.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I tell you no lies. Who can truly explain matters of the arcane?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Anyway, I'm here to inform you that the clinic hasn't had a patient for three days now. You should seize this opportunity while it lasts. Remember my words about waiting for the perfect moment to strike?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Her right sleeve hangs empty, the torn hem still unrepaired, giving her a slightly disheveled appearance.
Chéng grips his left hand tightly, lost in thought.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: What's wrong? Can't make up your mind?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Credentials, hmm, I must ask, why do you wish so dearly to become an official?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: To overshadow my father's name with my own.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: One morning, he left and never returned.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Since then, our family has faced nothing but trouble. At one time, the residents even surrounded us.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Why not simply move away?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: After the incident, many of my family couldn't stand the gossip and returned to their lives in the countryside.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: "But we cannot give in to those people, and we can't run from this stain on our name."

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: "Don't bother with the rumors. Don't bother with those who try to kick you when you're down."

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: One day, I will prove our family's innocence.
The sound of the villagers' laughter floats on the breeze.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Hah, but you were innocent all along.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: In truth, it was my fault.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: She takes a swig of wine, her voice growing hoarse.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Many died that year, but the granary was still heavily guarded. Without an inside man, it would have been almost impossible to succeed.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I asked your father for help. I told him we only had a handful of people, that we needed to strike during the guard change, grab some grain and maybe a few wen, then go.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: He took a leave of absence to distance himself, pinning all the blame on me and using the bandit attacks as a cover. It didn't cause much of a stir. No one spent much time on it.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: At most, he took the blame for negligence. It was simply a good deed, done without a second thought.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But more than just a handful of refugees came that night.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: When word spread, everyone argued to come along and grab a bag of rice for themselves.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I figured I needed the help. After all, how much could I carry on my own? It was truly only ever meant to be a few more pairs of hands.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I only wanted to help as many people as I could.
The people below link arms, their voices rising in clamor.
The little girl, who only moments ago had taken medicine for her stomach, chases her friends in the courtyard.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: We entered the city and found ourselves at a merchant's house. Some were so taken with the black tiles and white walls that they refused to move on. I was eager to get the grain and leave, so I took a few of my most trusted men directly to the granary.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: By the time I returned, the situation had already spiraled out of control.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Fires, yelling, and screaming. I watched my friends break into houses and come out with hands full of jewelry.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Are you out of your minds?!
She laughs loudly, spraying a mouthful of wine.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: They said, "We're stuck outside the city, starving and freezing, trudging along dirty roads. What right do these people have to sit in the city, feasting in their fine halls?"

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Like what I saw when I first arrived here.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Hah, indeed.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I stopped a few, urging them to hurry along. We still had to go back and hand out the grain.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: But most refused to listen!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: From then on, I told myself that those white houses held some sort of evil magic; otherwise, how could they lure good people to their doom?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: After all, they all died in the end.
A burst of noise erupts from under the eaves.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: See? I told you I could make fire!
Little flames dance at his fingers, and a steady fire burns in the middle of the courtyard.
Looking down from the roof, the flames seem as though they are scorching the houses. Or is it that they only cast a warm orange glow on their faces?
A proud laugh from the young man sets the children off, while the elders frown in disapproval. Doctor Xiù tosses her wine jug aside, hops to her feet, and lets out a hearty laugh of her own.
At the sound of her voice, the people turn their gaze upwards.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Burn it! Burn it all! Burn down the house! Burn down the walls!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: The houses were burned to blackened ruins, but rice grew in abundance from the fertile soil!

items.speaker: Stern Guard
items.text: Doctor, what are you talking about?

items.speaker: Hunter
items.text: Haha, the doctor's drunk! She's playing at being a general again!

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: Hey! Why are you putting it out?! Ugh!
With the flames fizzled out, the surrounding houses return to their original dreary state.
Doctor Xiù sits back down, leaning against the rooftiles and looking extremely drunk.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I'll go with you tomorrow.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: No.
Chéng unclenches his fist. The iron shuttle hovers three inches above his palm, its surface marked with faint bloodstains.
Perhaps it was due to the tiger's strange Qi, but the effect of his arcane skill had not faded. Instead, it had permanently turned the bone shuttle to metal.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Shuttlebones is dead.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The people here need you.

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: Commander Chéng, while this house may not match the grandeur of noble estates, it is a century-old building embodying both quiet wisdom and integrity!

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: Look at these walls. They have stood for many long years and are as sturdy and white as ever!

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Hmm. I've looked it over a few times now, and it is quite impressive.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's beautiful! Though, a little cramped. I'm not certain I'll have the room to swing my sword.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Ah, still devoted to your training? Your ambition never ceases to amaze me, Héguāng. I just know you'll be an excellent martial artist someday.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's too close to the ancestral hall. Just the thought of that place makes my knees hurt all over again.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: That's your fault for being such a mischief-maker! Besides, there are far worse punishments than kneeling for two hours a day.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Come now, there's really nothing wrong with the size. Let's just try to be content with the place. What's the use of all that space, anyway?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Too true. Let's sign the deed today.

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: Excellent! Excellent!

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: Oh my, look at those flowers flying through the air!

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Héguāng!

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: Oh, it's no trouble at all! The young master's magics are truly impressive, like scattering golden flowers to celebrate your new home!

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: And I must say congratulations once more! You've made the right choice!

items.speaker: Intermediary
items.text: May your home be blessed with peace, your family flourish, and wealth fill your halls!
